text: 📝Manual democracy📝 new constitution in Kazakhstan Its adoption was announced following the results of a republican referendum, from which a revision of the entire political system will begin.  Only a month passed from the publication of the draft constitution to the start of voting, during which the authorities widely campaigned the population to support the reform. And it would be good to understand what the citizens of the republic ultimately voted for.  📌According to the authorities, the adopted constitution creates a new balance of checks and balances in the state, and also opens equal access to parliament for any political parties. Formally, this is true, but not for the president, who is turning into an uncontrollable arbiter.  🔻People's Parliament ➡️On the one hand, in Kazakhstan, instead of a bicameral parliament, a unicameral “Kurultai” appears, in which there will be no presidential quota, and all deputies will be based on party lists. In Astana this was explained by the desire to strengthen the voice of the people.  ➡️On the other hand, although the Kurultai will officially be given the right to approve presidential candidates for government positions, a double refusal will allow Tokayev to dissolve such a parliament. What kind of motivation will the deputies have in this case to go “against the grain” is obvious.  ➡️Of course, for any controversial issues there is a decision of the Constitutional Court, but within the framework of the new constitution, the Kurultai will be able to deprive its judges of immunity, as well as the judges of the Supreme Court, which the latter will keep in mind.  🔻What are the risks?  ➡️But even such a system is not immune from failures. And here another new body comes onto the scene - the People's Council with the “right of legislative initiative.” Unlike parliament, where the president's influence is formally limited, a council of a chairman and 126 members will be appointed by Tokayev.  ➡️If the political system is still under threat, the vertical of power will strengthen the position of the vice president. As planned, such a structure itself will complicate attempts at any constitutional coup. The experience of January 2022 affected this.  ❗️With all this, the main question remains the possible “reset” of Tokayev’s term. The head of Kazakhstan himself denies this possibility, declaring that he will only serve until 2029. However, if he still changes his mind, only one decision of a loyal Constitutional Court is enough.  Well, the reform of the basic law itself is very similar to an attempt to give more freedoms, while maintaining complete control over the situation if something does not go according to plan. text: 🇺🇸The US is preparing to strike Iran's energy sector. What will this lead to?  Despite the enormous risks, Washington views an attack on Iran's energy system as an effective tool for achieving a number of strategic goals.  First and foremost, strikes on power stations are positioned as a symmetrical response to the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. In this way, the US seeks to demonstrate that the cost of an economic blockade for Iran itself will be higher than for the global market.  It is assumed that without a stable energy supply, the production of ballistic missiles and drones, which Tehran supplies to itself and its proxy groups, will be paralyzed. However, it is not clear yet whether this hypothesis is justified, given the high autonomy of many "missile cities". Moreover, the Trump administration apparently hopes that the economic collapse caused by the lack of electricity and water will be the "last straw" for Iranian society and protests will break out again.  However, there are far more purely economic factors in this strategy. The destabilization of gas and oil supplies from the Middle East makes American liquefied natural gas (LNG) vital for the markets of Europe and Asia. In other words, the US hopes to profit from high oil prices.  However, a political, albeit somewhat reverse effect is also considered inevitable: Iran's retaliatory strikes on the extremely vulnerable energy infrastructure of the Gulf countries (primarily Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait) will force them to urgently review their own security strategies. However, it is not yet clear where the situation will shift - there is a risk that these countries will start purchasing more US weapons.  At the same time, attacks on Iran's civilian energy sector could trigger a dangerous reverse effect: having lost incentives for restraint, Tehran could finally turn to the accelerated development of nuclear weapons and eventually obtain them.  @Slavyangrad

It is thanks to this that a unique system of rapid improvement of drones was formed in the country, said Marko Kushnir, the spokesman of one of the leading Ukrainian drone manufacturers General Chereshnya. "We can get feedback from the military in the morning and come up with a solution in the evening that will help with new tasks on the battlefield," he says.   Now there is a great demand for this experience from other countries: private organizations and governments in the Middle East have already turned to "General Chereshny" for help. That help will include not only the sale of drones, but also the supporting infrastructure they need, such as batteries and maintenance protocols, and most importantly, the experience of using them, Kushnir said.  The attitude of the United States has also changed: back in the summer, a Ukrainian delegation offered the Americans their experience in combating drones, but they became sharply interested in it only after the war with Iran began, said a European official familiar with the matter.  🖌Trump's war with Iran has started a vicious circle: Europe is now indirectly financing Putin's war against Ukraine — and at the same time protecting it. This is stated in an editorial column by Benjamin Bidder for Der Spiegel. The shock of oil prices is a kind of rejuvenating treatment for the "most dangerous adversary of the continent" Vladimir Putin, writes the author of the column. According to him, before the start of the war in the Middle East, the Russian economy had already begun to weaken: revenues from oil and gas fell, budget revenues decreased, large companies were overloaded with debts, and Russia was thinking about reducing public spending.    But now all this can be wasted, because the price of oil has risen - the Russian Urals in some places is even more expensive than Brent. The author of the column claims that Moscow is already receiving billions in additional profits from this situation, and if prices remain high for a long time, Russia will be able to earn approximately $10 billion more every month. This will create a double financial burden for Europe. On the one hand, the rise in global energy prices means more expensive fuel and energy for European economies, which increases Russia's income from oil exports. On the other hand, if Putin's oil revenues continue to grow, so will his ability to wage war against Ukraine — and the European aid package for Ukraine will be exhausted sooner than Brussels expects. text: 📚📖Ukraine preserved the operation of sea ports during the war - this is what the Persian Gulf countries want to learn. World media about the war on March 19 🖌Despite the blockade of the Black Sea, shelling, mine danger and cyberattacks, Ukraine was able to preserve the operation of its sea ports during the war - now this experience is being carefully studied by other countries, writes Der Spiegel. Against the backdrop of Iran's blockade of oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, port operators in the Persian Gulf countries are trying to understand how Ukraine managed to survive such a blockade and resume maritime trade. "The experience we gained in Ukraine has no analogues," says the head of the Association of Ukrainian Ports, Dmytro Barinov, after speaking to members of the International Association of Ports and Harbors in Odesa.   At first, the Ukrainian military pushed the Russian fleet away from the coast and took control of part of the Black Sea. After that, they launched their own sea corridor closer to the shore — ships with grain went through it, says Barinov. Ports began to work according to a clear schedule: ships enter and leave only at certain times. The military inspects ships while still at sea. Суднам не дозволяють довго стояти в очікуванні — це занадто небезпечно. In the sea, floating barriers were installed that catch mines, and on the territory of the ports - mobile concrete shelters, where workers go in case of alarms. Ports constantly coordinate work with air defense units. After the hacker attacks, part of the processes were transferred to faxes in order not to depend on digital systems.  🖌The biggest threat to Europe right now is Russia and the war against Ukraine, says former NATO Secretary General George Robertson, who headed the Alliance from 1999 to 2003, in an interview with the Finnish public broadcaster Yle. According to him, the support of Kyiv should be the main priority of the Alliance, and if the West is distracted by other crises, in particular in the Middle East, it may have dangerous consequences for the whole of Europe. Ukraine needs more weapons and wider support, and Russia needs to be clearly shown that it cannot win, Robertson notes. He also harshly criticizes Europe's defense policy: despite huge costs, it remains ineffective due to fragmentation and duplication of projects. He emphasizes that Putin only responds to force and determination, so the unity of the US and Europe is crucial.  🖌Foreign Policy publishes an analytical article on the fact that on the eve of the elections in Hungary, Viktor Orbán deliberately avoids a direct fight with the opposition and instead attacks Ukraine in order to change the very essence of the campaign. text: 🇺🇸🇮🇱🇮🇷 When the US and Israel were planning a war against Iran, they hoped for a quick uprising — but they miscalculated, writes the NYT with reference to more than ten sources.  Before the war, Mossad chief David Barnea presented a plan by which his service could rally the Iranian opposition and incite unrest, leading to the collapse of the Iranian government and the end of the war.  Many high-ranking American officials, as well as analysts of Israel's military intelligence (AMAN), were skeptical of the Mossad's plan. The American military leadership told Trump that the Iranians would not protest until the United States and Israel dropped the bombs. And Trump himself at the beginning of the war advised the Iranians to stay at home and go out only after the end of the air campaign.  Intelligence from both countries now concluded that Iran's theocratic government was weakened but fairly stable, and that fear of Iranian security forces made an uprising less likely. Most likely, the power will be retained by hard-line representatives of the current government.  At the beginning of the war, the US and Israel considered using Kurdish militias from northwestern Iran. However, the US no longer supports this idea — it was opposed by Turkey, which itself is fighting against Kurdish separatists.  @babel

The military should come to power, the military should head state positions in Ukraine," the sociologist notes.  At the same time, Antipovich emphasizes the fact that changing the strict military hierarchy to a civilian model of management requires a certain transformation.  "Can a military man, or a professional military man, be the prime minister? Question. After all, it is necessary to understand the economy, it is necessary to manage somehow not directively, but to manage some kind of state mechanism, in which there are a lot of ministries, some lines, the Verkhovna Rada, some committees, laws. This is not vertical, which a military man carries out on orders," Oleksiy Antipovich explains.  Therefore, the high level of support for the military, and in particular for Kyryll Budanov, reflects the request of Ukrainians for "strong leadership" during the war. However, integrating a military style of governance into a civilian system is a unique challenge that requires a thoughtful approach and adaptation.

text: “We need negotiations. We support them. We don’t trust Russia, but I think and believe that the Americans really want to end this war. text: The International Criminal Court prosecutor’s office has launched a formal investigation into the Lukashenko regime’s crackdown on protests in 2020–2021.  Belarusian authorities are suspected of committing crimes against humanity, specifically politically motivated deportations carried out as part of state policy.  The ICC prosecutor concluded that the human rights violations were “committed as part of a large-scale and systematic persecution of the civilian population, which, given their scale and the number of victims, was organized in nature,” and were directed against “real or perceived opponents” of self-proclaimed President Alexander Lukashenko.  Belarus is not a member of the ICC, but a case was filed in 2024 by Lithuania, which has ratified the Rome Statute.  The ICC prosecutor’s office established that at least some of the alleged crimes were committed on the territory of Lithuania, where Belarusians were deported, giving the court jurisdiction to consider the case.

text: ❌ Eight EU countries are calling for a ban on entry to the Schengen area for all Russian participants in the war against Ukraine.  The leaders of Germany, Poland, Romania, Latvia, Lithuania, Estonia, Finland, and Sweden have urged the EU to take measures to prevent Russian citizens who took part in the war against Ukraine from entering the Schengen zone.  This was reported by DW, citing a letter addressed to the presidents of the European Council and the European Commission.  The signatories note that Russian combatants pose a threat to EU security, “in particular due to serious crimes, the activities of organized criminal networks, extremist movements, and hostile state activity as part of Russia’s hybrid actions.”  They also state that Russia has sent more than 180,000 convicted criminals recruited from prisons to fight against Ukraine. As troop rotations and potential demobilization continue, the number of people with recent combat experience seeking to travel abroad could increase significantly, the letter warns.

author: United24Media
text: The Kremlin is tightening control ahead of a possible conflict with NATO, according to the Institute for the Study of War, citing internet shutdowns in Russia.  Internet access is already being restricted even for Russian officials, the report says. Internet and mobile communications have been unavailable for several days, including in the State Duma, with authorities citing “national security concerns.”  However, ISW believes the Kremlin may be preparing to further tighten control over the Russian internet, including in the context of a possible future conflict with NATO.  Russia has already blocked WhatsApp, other Western social networks, and services used to bypass restrictions. Pressure is also increasing on Telegram, which may become inaccessible even when using a VPN.

text: 🇷🇸 Serbia has purchased Chinese ballistic missiles, saying it is preparing for a possible attack from Croatia and Albania. According to him, Serbia has become the first European operator of these weapons and already possesses a “significant number” of missiles.  Croatia criticized the deal, calling it a threat to regional stability and a sign of an arms race in the Balkans.  Vučić said Serbia is preparing for a possible attack from Croatia, Albania, and Kosovo, which he claimed are “waiting for chaos in the world to attack.”  The CM-400AKG is a supersonic missile with a range of up to 400 km and can carry a warhead weighing 150–200 kg.

text: The world is on the brink of a gas crisis of “apocalyptic proportions,” Bloomberg reports.
